Creator seeding is sending free product to TikTok Shop creators in the hope they post about it, and the difference between seeding that works and seeding that wastes product is entirely in the process. Curate a tight list, make a real offer, track every box, and follow up. Do that and a seeding wave becomes your affiliate roster. Skip it and you are mailing samples into a void.

Step 1: Build a curated list, not a big one

Target 15 to 25 creators for your first wave, all of whom sell in your category. Quantity is not the goal; fit is. A focused list of proven category sellers outperforms a hundred random recipients, because affiliate GMV is concentrated in the few who actually convert.

Vet before you ship: category selling history, posting consistency, real engagement, audience match. See how to vet creators.

Step 2: Make the offer worth posting for

Seeding is not just free product. Pair the sample with a competitive commission so the creator has an ongoing reason to sell, not just a one-off unboxing. When you are new, lean toward a stronger commission to earn the post.

Reach out through Target Collaboration with a short, specific message. Templates in creator outreach.

Step 3: Ship and track every box

The unglamorous part that decides the outcome. Track who you shipped to, when it arrived, and whether they posted. A simple spreadsheet or a CRM works. Boxes that arrive and get forgotten are the single biggest source of seeding waste.

Step 4: Follow up

Most creators will not post from the box alone. A polite follow-up once product arrives, with the hook and offer restated, dramatically lifts post rates. This is where casual seeding loses and systematic seeding wins.

Step 5: Double down on responders

Expect a long tail of silence. Many seeded creators will never post, and that is normal. Your job is to spot the ones who do post and sell, then invest in them: more product, better commission, bigger collaborations. A handful of responders will drive most of your GMV.

The sellers who scale say the unglamorous part is what compounds. In a r/TikTokshop thread on what got people past five figures a month, one seller doing "95k GMV last month" credited "consistency and investing enough into your business so you have what your customers want or ask for on hand" (r/TikTokshop). Seeding only pays off if you can fulfill the demand your responders create, so pair every wave with the inventory to back it.

What good seeding looks like in numbers

  • A first wave of 15 to 25 curated creators.
  • A minority who post; a smaller minority who sell well.
  • Fast reinvestment in the sellers, and a fresh wave to replace the silent ones.

Seeding is a repeatable engine, not a one-time blast. Run waves continuously, keep the winners, replace the non-responders, and your active roster compounds.

The takeaway

Seeding works when it is a tracked, followed-up, curated process aimed at proven category sellers, and fails when it is a pile of samples mailed and forgotten. The logistics are boring and they are exactly what separates results from waste.

Want seeding run as a system for you? Book a call, or build a target list of category sellers to seed.
